prompt:
You describe a timing diagram from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. Every signal, from top to bottom.
2. The sequence of edges and states in time order, and which edge triggers which.
3. Every named interval (for example tSU, tH) with its value and unit, if shown.

Figure type: timing diagram
Section: 10 4-wire Serial Configuration and Data Interface > 10.5 FIFO Access
Caption: Figure 16: SRES Command Strobe
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): SI HeaderSRES HeaderAddr Data SO | CSn
Text that mentions the figure: A command strobe may be followed by any other SPI access without pulling CSn high. However, if an SRES strobe is being issued, one will have to wait for SO to go low again before the next header byte can be issued as shown in Figure 16. The command strobes are executed immediately, with the exception of the SPWD, SWOR, and the SXOFF strobes, which are executed when CSn goes high.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Timing diagram from Figure 16: SRES Command Strobe.

Signals from top to bottom are CSn, SO, and SI.

The sequence of edges and states in time order is as follows:
- CSn starts high and goes low.
- SI transitions to HeaderSRES.
- SI transitions to HeaderAddr.
- SI transitions to Data.
- SO goes high, then goes low.
- CSn goes high.

Named intervals are not shown in the figure.
